correctness.rationale: Finite n: the transformed maximum density has the endpoint power n alpha-1 and an exponential right tail, so its entropy and mean are finite. With r=1/sigma, optimizing out mu gives mu=-log E exp(-rY_n)/r and profile second derivative r^-2 plus tilted variance. For large r, the positive probability of an interval within any delta of the lower endpoint gives a linear lower bound on the profile choosing delta<mean minus endpoint; -log r gives coercivity at 0. This proves global uniqueness. Asymptotics: writing c=alpha-1, b=b_n and epsilon=c/b^2, exact reciprocal-hazard normalization cancels the linear tail error. The variable psi(y)=-log(n S(b+a_n y)) satisfies psi=y+epsilon y^2/2+O(b^-3(1+|y|^3)) and psi'=1+epsilon y+O(b^-3(1+y^2)) on the window. The maximum density there agrees with g(psi)psi' up to negligible finite-n error, hence p_n/g=1+epsilon s+O(b^-3 polylog(b)). I checked the growing-window step independently: on the left with x=b+a_n y>=b/2 the normalized hazard is 1+O(1/b) uniformly, so nS is between exp((1-O(1/b))|y|) and exp((1+O(1/b))|y|). The CDF bound makes any fixed exponential/polynomial weight and the log-density term negligible there. For x<b/2, T=-n log F(M_n) is exactly Exp(1), with T at least exp(b/3) on that region for large b. This controls (n-1)|log F(M_n)| directly; at x<1 the bound F(x)<=C x^alpha controls |log x| by a constant plus T/(n alpha). All other left cross-entropy/score weights on this region grow at most exponentially in b. The right tail has density bounded by C exp(-0.85 y) and log density ratio O(1+y). Thus tail masses, entropy terms and needed derivative moments are negligible relative to b^-4, with the derivative bounds uniform on a compact parameter neighborhood of (0,1). Normalization cancels the first KL Taylor term; the standard-fit leading loss is epsilon^2 E[s^2]/2. The inverse-scale profile derivative converges locally, has J_n'(1)=O(epsilon), and has locally positive slope bounded away from zero, putting the unique global optimizer at (0,1)+O(epsilon). Expanding cross-entropy there gives gradient -epsilon v+o(epsilon) and Hessian I+o(1), so the minimizing displacement is epsilon I^-1 v+o(epsilon). For an independent coefficient check use T[A]=(1-e^-y)A-A'; s=T[-y^2/2], and the two scores are T[1],T[y]. Integration by parts gives inner product E_g[A'B'+e^-Y A B]. Under weight e^-Y the variable e^-Y has Gamma(2,1) law. Setting h=EulerGamma-1 and q=y-h orthogonalizes 1 and q, with norms squared 1,zeta(2). For -q^2/2 the two inner products are -(zeta(2)-1)/2 and -zeta(3); its squared norm is 1+zeta(2)+[3(zeta(2)-1)^2+6(zeta(4)-1)]/4. Restoring the shift gives the displayed location/scale coefficients. The residual half-norm is (zeta(2)^2+3 zeta(4))/4-zeta(3)^2/(2 zeta(2)), yielding the claimed constant. It is positive because a quadratic transport cannot coincide in this positive norm with a linear one. Independent high-precision evaluation gives fitted 1.0489851103816137536, unfitted 1.2118030275885142504, location -0.5420488725547554046, scale -0.3079786343029713593. The argument uses fixed alpha, and neither an alpha approaching one nor reversed KL fits these conclusions.

originality.rationale: Credit the first nonvanishing optimized forward-KL asymptotic for fixed nonexponential Gamma shapes, including its projection loss and parameter shifts under exact reciprocal-hazard normalization. Do not credit usual Gamma norming, entropy convergence without a sharp rate, generic KL Taylor geometry, or exponential-parent fitting. The strongest inspected published passages have the same entropy convergence problem or the same fitting operation but do not dominate the claimed sharp nonexponential result. This is a best-of-knowledge assessment, not historical priority certification.
residual_risks: Inaccessible Gamma norming and penultimate papers or an uninspected general sharp projection theorem could affect historical coverage.

value.rationale: This answers a concrete information-theoretic rate question beyond convergence, resolves whether affine fitting can remove the leading hazard-curvature error, and quantifies both the improvement and a strictly positive irreducible residual. The uniform expression across fixed nonexponential shapes and the contrasted exponential endpoint make the coefficient a useful benchmark for higher-order extreme-value calibration rather than a numerical constant chosen in isolation.
residual_risks: Fixed shape only; the result does not determine a transition when alpha approaches one with n, or calibration in non-Gumbel families.
